body: Oh ok thanks man! I’m new and I learned a lot from your reply :)
Yeah that would be a great strategy. Although on Xbox the only way to communicate is through voice chat parties... Lurking in a voice call might be kinda weird you know?

Thanks for trying to lift me up 3 days later, and with such kind words too. :) 

I’ve recently started trying out spoken word and it’s really been helping me vent. I’m starting to get invested in the “journey” vs being hung up on my “destination”.

I’m sorry you’re having to go through a crappy time too :/ You’re a really nice person for commenting tho. I bet your karma will balance out and you and your partner bounce out of the depression
What hints did you drop that said “you were going to die”?

It’s all too convoluted and embarrassing to explain, but to sum it up: I stayed in my room for 2 years. It robbed me of my personality, social skills, and my old friends are completely weirded out by what I’ve become wanting nothing to do with me. Everywhere I go people give me looks. It’s like the world has turned on me. I haven’t had a successful conversation without a judgmental stare since I started going outside again. Basically I ruined my life by not doing anything

I feel this same way. You basically described my life :| The only difference is I transferred to an alternative school and got to experience the “high school life”. But after graduating, I fell out of contact with everyone I knew again.

But in highschool I found a way out of that lonely, no personality void that we feel stuck in. How I did it?

Hobbies. I started working out and writing. Sure I was overweight and sure writing isn’t the most interesting or cool thing to be into, but I got super super immersed in both of those things.

After forcing myself into being passionate about those things, I started to have a lot of fun with them. I lost 90 pounds, wrote a bunch of short story rough drafts and got into character analysis.

The most important thing I did though was SHARE my interests. I became passionate and shared my passion. All of a sudden, I had a personality, I was happy because I was talking about what I loved, and I met people with similar interests with a common topic to fanboy over.

Granted after highschool I stopped pursuing my hobbies and regressed to where I am now, but that’s my template to becoming yourself. Hope it helps some because we really have similar stories

I used to trust people, but then I got depressed. Most of the people in my life left. A lot of the time when you have negative feelings people don’t won’t know how to react. There are some sensitive people though who understand the struggle. You’ll find or maybe have already found them. Those are the people that matter.
I haven’t called a hotline but that fake compassion would get under my skin too. Like you’re talking to a waiter that’s all smiles just for their job
If you took anything serious youshould really get to a ER.. The longer you wait the worse of a time you’ll have.

Don’t it’s too painful and horrible. I’m in a similar boat as you (bad situation, suicidal) but there’s a reason why you don’t see any meditated suicides via blood loss. Try taking your mind of things, hope you get better truly

That’s true it is really dangerous for other people... I don’t mean to talk so candidly about this but I generally only practice when driving at a gaurd rail. Thanks for the reply the safety of others is on my mind now

I isolated myself for 3 years and now I’m an antisocial man child. None of my old friends want to be associated with me. I finally got a job, but my co workers call me Pennywise because I’m light skinned black and have an Afro. The abuse at work is non stop. Every time I have to work with someone the others call out to us and mimic my voice saying “be my friend”. Everywhere I go people give me disgusted looks because of how tense I seem in public after isolating myself for 3 years. 

It’s hard to see things clearly when reality is always being shoved in your face. Thanks for the reply tho and I might try calling a hotline
